# WO-2026-08-14-01 — Warwick's names page, Mum's tiles, and the amber nudge

**Warwick's ruling, 2026-08-14, verbatim:** *"Go. Dispatch Felix now… Finish the editor, Mum tiles, amber
nudge and display-name sense-check."*

**`display_name` now EXISTS and is populated on live — 109 of 109 active regulars, zero falling back.**
Larry applied migration 021 and seeded it. So you are consuming a real field, not a planned one.

## THE THREE FIELDS — Warwick's own design. **No bleeding between them.**

| field | what it is | your use of it |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | the official ASDA listing. **The truth about the product** | **small line at the bottom of Mum's tile**, and shown in Warwick's editor |
| `aka` | what Mum writes on her lists. **A MATCHING TERM** | **NEVER displayed.** Not on her tile, not in your editor's edit field |
| `display_name` | **what Mum reads** | **the large line on her tile**, and the one editable field |

**⛔ `display_name` IS PRESENTATION ONLY.** Warwick's words: *"it must never feed display_name into
catalogue resolution or mutate matching behaviour."* Nothing you build may send it anywhere that decides
what a written line means.

## Acceptance criteria

**AC1 — Mum's tile: display name large, ASDA name small underneath.**
Warwick: *"on mums dashboard we should have the display name large and then the official asda name quite
small running in one line at the bottom of the tile, so its easy for me to see what it actually is."*
- `display_name` is the name. **`householdName()`'s `aka` fallback is retired** — `aka` must not reach her
  screen at all. Fall back to `name` only if `display_name` is somehow absent.
- The ASDA line is **one line**, small, and **must not wrap or push the tile** — it is orientation for
  Warwick, not reading matter for her. **Truncate it rather than let it grow the row.**
- **⚠️ Addendum B §6.3 sets a 22px floor and says a sub-line is "omitted rather than filled with a
  reference".** Warwick has overruled that for this line and his ruling governs — **but the floor is
  Vera's at re-gate. Tell her in your handoff what size you used and why**, and do not go below 22px
  without saying so explicitly.

**AC2 — the amber nudge.** Warwick tested the live page and said the nudge *"is grey and doesn't really
stand out."* He chose **amber, bold, with a left rail** over red — **because red already means the failed
send on this surface**, and a nudge is not a failure. Use the existing `--warn` / `--warn-w` tokens; **do
not invent one.**

**AC3 — Warwick's names page. `names.html` + `names.js` + `names.css`, on the OPERATOR cockpit.**
**⛔ NOT reachable from Mum's page and never linked from it.**
- Lists all 109 active regulars: **`display_name` (editable) · the ASDA `name` (read-only) · nothing else.**
- Saves via **`POST /api/asdair/display-name` `{ id, display_name }`** — the route exists and is live.
  Clearing the field sends `null`.
- **Show the 11 collision groups Larry flagged**, inline, with *why* — three Sure deodorants, three
  toffees, two egg boxes, two Vanish, two Febreze, two beef, two Batchelors, two bean products, BOB milk
  vs Cravendale, the cat litter guess, and row 51. Source: `Deliverables/2026-08-13-mum-display-names-DECISIONS.md`.
- **He is on a phone.** Big targets, one column, no modal, saves without leaving the row.
- **⛔ NEVER show or edit `aka`.** Editing it would change matching, which is the whole reason this field exists.

**AC4 — this is a hobby tool, not a product. Build it plainly.**
No optimistic UI, no undo stack, no autosave debouncing cleverness, no offline queue. **Save, show it
saved, show it plainly if it failed.** Warwick can retype. **A page with fewer moving parts is the correct
answer here** — the last package was simplified mid-build for exactly this reason.

## Required evidence

- `node services/cockpit/shopping-geometry-check.mjs` and `--self-test` and `--send-cases` → real counts.
  **Baseline: 104 states / 0 violations · 16/16 mutations, control clean · 13/13.** A fall in coverage is
  a regression and must be explained.
- `node services/cockpit/render-vm-check.mjs` → real counts. **Baseline 64 scenarios / 232 assertions.**
- `bash scripts/secret-scan.sh --surface <your paths>` → exit code AND coverage. Exit 2 is NOT SCANNED.
- **Your names page needs its own proof, and it need not be elaborate:** render it, drive one save through
  a stub, show the saved and failed states. **Do not build a third gate harness for it.**

## Inputs supplied

- `Deliverables/2026-08-13-mum-display-names-DECISIONS.md` — the 11 groups and why each needs Warwick.
- `services/asdair/cockpit-api/displayName.js` — the live write route.
- Addendum B §6.3 (tile and sub-line), §5.1, §10 — and Warwick's override of the sub-line rule.
- Vera's accepted narrowings and her outstanding recorded items: **MEDIUM-E** (`elaborateBelow` missing
  from `REST`), **MEDIUM-F** (mutation catch-counts do not identify which assertion fired), **MEDIUM-G**
  (small viewports never tested at realistic list length), **L1**. **Fix any that are cheap while you are
  in the file; none is required.**

## Explicitly out of scope — report, never fix

- **The duplicate sense-check against display names is KEEL's**, in parallel under WP-B15-53. Your nudge
  renders whatever `matched_name` the route returns. **Do not implement matching in the page.**
- `services/asdair/**`, `server.mjs`, `provenance.mjs`, `render-check.mjs`.
- The live services. Larry restarts them.

## Sequencing

1. **READ-BACK AND HOLD.** Short is fine. **Name the distribution path again** — your names page is a NEW
   file on a service with a service worker, and last time you established `SHELL` does not cache
   `shopping.*`. Say whether `names.*` inherits that or not, *before* building.
2. AC1 → AC2 → AC3, AC4 throughout.
3. **⛔ DO NOT COMMIT, DO NOT PUSH, DO NOT CREATE A BRANCH.** Your contract declares no integration role.
   Write the files in `C:/Fusion247PKA-dispui` and hand back the list. **Larry commits.**

**Standing constraints:** never checks out, never pays, never chooses a slot. **Do not message Mum or
anyone.** And Warwick has been explicit that this is not enterprise software — *"there's only me and mum
using it, don't go mental with the edge cases."*
